name: academic-figure-skills
description: AI-powered academic figure generation skill pack — parse papers, analyze code repos, plan figures, generate publication-quality prompts with colorblind-safe palettes
author: Azhi-ss

skills.name: Academic Figure Workflow Orchestrator
skills.description: Use when the user wants an end-to-end academic figure workflow, wants to go from a repository or paper to a figure prompt, or is unsure which academic-figure skill to start with.
trigger_phrases: 帮我从仓库到配图走一遍
which skill should I use first

skills.name: Academic Repo Analyzer
skills.description: Use when the user wants to analyze a deep learning or machine learning code repository, understand what it does, identify its architecture and tech stack, or generate a quick understanding document for downstream figure planning.

skills.name: Academic Figure Prompt
skills.description: Use when the user wants detailed English prompts for AI image tools to produce top-conference-quality academic figures in the classic academic style, including framework, architecture, module-detail, comparison, and data-pattern diagrams.

skills.name: Academic Figure Prompt — Modern ML Airy Style
skills.description: Use when the user wants modern ML or RL paper-style figure prompts matching ICLR, NeurIPS, or ICML 2024-2025 aesthetics, especially with a soft pastel academic diagram style.

skills.name: Academic Paper Analyzer & Figure Planner
skills.description: Use when the user wants to analyze an academic paper, identify figure-worthy content, and plan which figures to generate by section.
trigger_phrases: which figures does my paper need

skills.name: Academic Figure Color Expert
skills.description: Use when the user wants help choosing an academic figure color palette, needs venue-specific or colorblind-safe design advice, or wants a paper color scheme recommendation.

skills.name: Academic Skill Eval Team
skills.description: Use when the user wants to evaluate a skill or skill pack with an agent team, audit trigger phrases, inspect workflow completeness, score output quality, or stress-test prompt robustness before release.
